title: Phased Rollout Engine for Batch + Cache Tunings (shadow testing & canary rollback)
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal: Build a phased rollout engine that can safely apply continuous batching and cache parameter changes to live workloads by using shadow testing, canary traffic, conservative parameter annealing, and automated rollback triggers. The engine should integrate with the workload profiler, cost telemetry, and the runtime's KV cache heuristics so we can realize per-token cost savings without impacting latency SLOs or correctness.

Scope and success criteria:
- Implement a rollout controller that accepts candidate parameter sets (batch size limits, coalescence window, KV warming thresholds, prefix cache TTLs, quantization profile hints) produced by the recommender pipeline.
- Provide three rollout modes: shadow-only (no production traffic impact), canary (small % traffic), and staged (incremental percent increases).
- Safety checks: latency P95 regression guard, error-rate spike detection, and token-cost delta threshold. Rollback is automatic when any guard trips.
- Telemetry: per-canary cohort metrics surfaced in Console (latency, tail, cost-per-token, throughput, cache hitrate).
- Integration: hook into workload fingerprinting service (ENG-612345) and batching profiler.
- Deliverable: engine + operator docs + runbook for oncall + 2 example safe-rollouts applied to internal model routes.

Trade-offs and design decisions considered:
1) Aggressiveness vs safety: we choose conservative annealing by default (max change 10% per stage) to limit risk for stateful KV cache behavior. This sacrifices fastest convergence for reduced rollback frequency.
2) Shadow fidelity: shadow mode replays real requests to candidate config in a lightweight isolated runtime to measure correctness and cache behavior. To reduce cost we sample 1-2% of traffic for full replay and use synthetic synthetic-prefix probes for cold-cache behavior.
3) Rollback triggers complexity: initial implementation uses simple threshold-based triggers (latency P95 +20% over baseline OR error-rate x2 OR cost-per-token increase > 5%). Future work may replace with statistical significance testing or Bayesian regret estimates.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 0 (spike, 2w): validate shadow replay architecture; prototype lightweight replay harness and gather baseline signals (latency, cache hit rate). Link: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/INF/Shadow+Replay+Spike
- Phase 1 (engine MVP, 3w): rollout controller + canary scheduler + simple guard rules + dashboard wiring. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1289
- Phase 2 (safety/operator UX, 2w): runbook, operator CLI, rollout history & rollback button in Console.
- Phase 3 (automation, 3w): tie recommender to automatic propose/apply loop with staged annealing; create audit/logging for compliance.

Runbook excerpt (automated rollback flow):
1) Canary created at 1% traffic. System records baseline window (last 30m).
2) Evaluate metrics every 60s; if P95 latency > baseline*1.2 for 3 consecutive windows -> automatic rollback.
3) If error-rate jumps above threshold or model outputs show structural regressions (via eval harness) -> immediate rollback and alert paging.

Open questions and risks:
- Cold-cache regression detection: how to simulate production-wide cold-cache scenarios reliably in shadow mode? Propose periodic synthetic prefix probes combined with low-rate full replays.
- Cost accounting for shadow: shadow replays consume GPU cycles; need billing treatment for internal tests vs customer chargeback. Suggest tagging shadow runs and excluding from external metrics.
- Interactions with dedicated deployments: ensure rollout controller respects tenant isolation and Dedicated autoscaling behaviors.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.company/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=design-872619
- Spike notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-A-example-spike-notes
- Example dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/canary-rollouts/872619

Notes on data retention and audit: every apply must be recorded with parameter diff, who requested, and deterministic seed for replay. Audit logs should be exportable for compliance teams.
